evidence.claim: Brazil's GDP grew 2.9% in 2022, with services up 4.2%, industry up 1.6%, and agriculture down 1.7%.
evidence.title: GDP grows 2.9% in 2022, closes the year at R$9.9 trillion
evidence.excerpt: Brazil's GDP grew 2.9% in 2022, with services up 4.2%, industry up 1.6%, and agriculture down 1.7%.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IBGE is the official national statistics agency and this is a standard GDP release with direct annual estimates.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 target year; published March 2023 with the final annual estimate.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual, not uniquely attributable to Bolsonaro; reflects the full-year macro record under his administration plus global and domestic conditions.
contrary_evidence: Growth remained uneven across sectors.
Does not by itself show ruler-driven prosperity gains.

evidence.claim: The average annual unemployment rate in 2022 was 9.3%, and employed population averaged 98.0 million, the highest annual average in the series.
evidence.title: Continuous PNAD: in 2022, average annual unemployment rate was 9.3%, average annual underutilization rate was 20.8%
evidence.excerpt: The average annual unemployment rate in 2022 was 9.3%, and employed population averaged 98.0 million, the highest annual average in the series.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IBGE is the official source for labor-market statistics and the release reports the annual series directly.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 and was published shortly after year-end.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual outcome under Bolsonaro's final year; not a direct policy effect by itself.
contrary_evidence: High unemployment and underemployment still persisted.
Does not isolate Bolsonaro-specific causation.

evidence.claim: Brazil's IPCA rose 5.79% in 2022, and food and beverages were a major contributor to December inflation.
evidence.title: IPCA was 0.62% in December, closes 2022 at 5.79%
evidence.excerpt: Brazil's IPCA rose 5.79% in 2022, and food and beverages were a major contributor to December inflation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IBGE is the official inflation statistician and the release reports the final annual CPI series.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 annual inflation outcome, published January 2023.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual macro outcome under Bolsonaro's final year; inflation was also shaped by global food and fuel shocks and monetary policy.
contrary_evidence: Inflation fell from 2021's 10.06% rate.
Lower inflation alone did not restore household purchasing power.

evidence.claim: The World Bank estimated that 30.7% of Brazil's population experienced moderate or severe food insecurity in 2022, and said food prices rose 37.5% between end-2019 and end-2022.
evidence.title: Inflação de alimentos e insegurança alimentar no Brasil
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank estimated that 30.7% of Brazil's population experienced moderate or severe food insecurity in 2022, and said food prices rose 37.5% between end-2019 and end-2022.
evidence.source_locator: Body text discussing 2022 food insecurity and prices
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank analysis is high-quality and explicitly links 2022 food insecurity to inflation and household welfare.
evidence.period_fit: Explicitly discusses 2022 conditions, with retrospective comparisons to 2019-2021.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly contextual, but relevant to policy because social protection and inflation responses during Bolsonaro's term affected household exposure.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes social-protection measures cushioned the worst pandemic-era losses.
The evidence does not isolate Bolsonaro from inherited pandemic effects.

evidence.claim: By mid-2022, annual inflation in Brazil was estimated at 13.9%, and food costs had risen 13.43% in the 12 months to August 2022.
evidence.title: Fighting against poverty: the impact of inflation on households’ purchasing power
evidence.excerpt: By mid-2022, annual inflation in Brazil was estimated at 13.9%, and food costs had risen 13.43% in the 12 months to August 2022.
evidence.source_locator: Opinion text / data paragraph on Brazil
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank staff commentary draws on contemporaneous price data and is directly tied to household welfare.
evidence.period_fit: Directly addresses 2022 price conditions, published in October 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual; reflects inflation that Bolsonaro's government tried to offset but did not fully control.
contrary_evidence: Nominal average labor incomes also rose, partly offsetting the shock.
The piece is analytic commentary, not a ruler-specific audit.

evidence.claim: Copom said the Russia-Ukraine war worsened inflationary pressures, warned that fiscal policies that worsen the future fiscal path could raise risk premia and de-anchor expectations, and kept tightening monetary policy.
evidence.title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee — Copom
evidence.excerpt: Copom said the Russia-Ukraine war worsened inflationary pressures, warned that fiscal policies that worsen the future fiscal path could raise risk premia and de-anchor expectations, and kept tightening monetary policy.
evidence.source_locator: Sections A, B, and D; paragraphs 1, 11, 12, 21-24
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Copom minutes are the primary record of Brazil's monetary-policy deliberations and the inflation-risk assessment in March 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and highly relevant to the macro environment Bolsonaro faced.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly contextual, because the central bank is independent; relevant mainly as a contemporaneous assessment of the policy environment Bolsonaro was governing.
contrary_evidence: The tightening cycle was executed by the independent central bank, not the president alone.
The minutes do not assign responsibility to Bolsonaro personally.

evidence.claim: Copom said Brazilian activity was growing above expectations and the labor market was recovering, but inflation remained high and broad-based, with food and fuel shocks still prominent.
evidence.title: Atas do Comitê de Política Monetária - Copom
evidence.excerpt: Copom said Brazilian activity was growing above expectations and the labor market was recovering, but inflation remained high and broad-based, with food and fuel shocks still prominent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary central-bank minutes documenting the state of the 2022 economy and inflation drivers.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual rather than directly attributable to Bolsonaro, but relevant to the administration's economic environment and response choices.
contrary_evidence: The central bank attributes some weakness to global and commodity shocks.
Positive output and labor recovery complicate any one-direction verdict.

evidence.claim: Copom said the labor market continued to recover, consumer inflation had recently been reduced by tax measures and lower fuel prices, but underlying inflation remained above the range compatible with the inflation target.
evidence.title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee — Copom
evidence.excerpt: Copom said the labor market continued to recover, consumer inflation had recently been reduced by tax measures and lower fuel prices, but underlying inflation remained above the range compatible with the inflation target.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: This is the primary monetary-policy record for October 2022 and directly documents the inflation dynamic.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual; the tax measures were part of the Bolsonaro government's policy mix, while monetary policy was independent.
contrary_evidence: Tax-driven disinflation can be temporary and fiscally costly.
Underlying inflation still remained elevated.

evidence.claim: Congress approved a spending package Bolsonaro was banking on for reelection that bypassed the spending cap and boosted social benefits, prompting investor concern about fiscal discipline and inflation.
evidence.title: Brazil Congress approves major spending bill, lifting Bolsonaro re-election hopes
evidence.excerpt: Congress approved a spending package Bolsonaro was banking on for reelection that bypassed the spending cap and boosted social benefits, prompting investor concern about fiscal discipline and inflation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is strong independent coverage, though the piece relies partly on market expectations and political context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct enough to Bolsonaro's reelection strategy because the package was explicitly tied to his campaign and administration.
contrary_evidence: Government said it needed urgent relief for households hit by inflation.
The package had congressional approval, not sole presidential unilateral action.

evidence.claim: Reuters estimated that Bolsonaro's 2022 election-year benefits and promises would cost R$273 billion in 2022-2023, with R$127.4 billion already approved and implemented.
evidence.title: SAIBA MAIS-Benefícios em série e promessas de Bolsonaro em ano eleitoral têm custo de R$273 bi em 2022 e 2023
evidence.excerpt: Reuters estimated that Bolsonaro's 2022 election-year benefits and promises would cost R$273 billion in 2022-2023, with R$127.4 billion already approved and implemented.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong independent source, and the UOL mirror preserves the original report and numbers.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to the election period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's election strategy and executive choices.
contrary_evidence: Some measures were already approved through Congress, not by executive fiat alone.
Short-term relief can be justified in inflationary periods, but fiscal sustainability is the counterpoint.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro said he expected deflation the following month because lower fuel prices after an ICMS tax change would reduce inflation.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro diz esperar deflação em agosto com queda no preço dos combustíveis
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro said he expected deflation the following month because lower fuel prices after an ICMS tax change would reduce inflation.
evidence.source_locator: Quoted remarks in the Reuters report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters captured the president's own public statement, which is reliable for the claim he made even if not for its predictive accuracy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential rhetoric and policy framing.
contrary_evidence: The effect was framed as temporary and dependent on tax changes.
Fuel-tax relief can also be fiscally costly and not structurally anti-inflationary.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro acknowledged inflation in food and fuel but blamed state governors and the war in Ukraine for the price surge.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro reconhece inflação, mas culpa estados e guerra na Ucrânia
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro acknowledged inflation in food and fuel but blamed state governors and the war in Ukraine for the price surge.
evidence.source_locator: Quoted remarks in the Reuters report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is reliable for contemporaneous public statements and the piece directly captures Bolsonaro's rhetoric.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential rhetoric, relevant to honesty and accountability for shocks.
contrary_evidence: Ukraine war and global commodity shocks were real external drivers.
The statement alone does not prove policy failure or success.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro issued a decree delegating to the Economy Minister authority over opening 2022 budget credits and related budget adjustments to speed execution.
evidence.title: Decreto prevê delegação de competências ao Ministro de Estado da Economia
evidence.publisher: Secretaria-Geral da Presidência / Governo do Brasil
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro issued a decree delegating to the Economy Minister authority over opening 2022 budget credits and related budget adjustments to speed execution.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: This is the official government announcement of an enacted decree with a clear administrative delegation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct and strong: this was a presidential decree under Bolsonaro's authority.
contrary_evidence: Delegation does not prove the minister was competent, only that he was empowered.
Budget execution still faced fiscal and inflationary constraints.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro signed a law extending payroll-tax relief through 2023 for 17 labor-intensive sectors, including construction, transport, and communications.
evidence.title: Presidente Bolsonaro sanciona Projeto de Lei da desoneração da folha de pagamento de 17 setores da economia
evidence.publisher: Secretaria-Geral da Presidência / Governo do Brasil
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro signed a law extending payroll-tax relief through 2023 for 17 labor-intensive sectors, including construction, transport, and communications.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official record of the enacted measure and its stated policy purpose.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022, though the law was signed at the start of the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action, though the measure originated in Congress and was framed as a jobs policy.
contrary_evidence: Sectoral tax relief can privilege connected industries rather than broad-based reform.
The measure creates revenue costs that have to be offset elsewhere.

evidence.claim: The government said the Investment Partnership Program would invest BRL 78 billion in 2022 and that commitments signed between 2019 and 2022 would exceed BRL 1.3 trillion over coming years.
evidence.title: Brazil's investments will exceed BRL 1.3 trillion in the coming years
evidence.excerpt: The government said the Investment Partnership Program would invest BRL 78 billion in 2022 and that commitments signed between 2019 and 2022 would exceed BRL 1.3 trillion over coming years.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official program summary is reliable for what the administration claimed and what commitments it reported, though not all downstream effects are independently verified here.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Bolsonaro's administration and its investment policy agenda.
contrary_evidence: This is a pipeline/commitment figure, not a measured welfare outcome.
Long-run effectiveness depends on execution and project quality.

evidence.claim: The PPI said it concluded 48 projects in 2022 and secured more than R$101 billion in contracted investments, including the Eletrobras capitalisation and airport concessions.
evidence.title: Secretaria Especial do PPI concluiu 48 projetos em 2022 e assegurou R$ 101 bilhões em novos investimentos
evidence.excerpt: The PPI said it concluded 48 projects in 2022 and secured more than R$101 billion in contracted investments, including the Eletrobras capitalisation and airport concessions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official year-end program report on completed projects and contracted investment, with clear implementation language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Bolsonaro administration's investment-policy execution, though project-level economics depend on private actors and regulators.
contrary_evidence: Contracted investments are not the same as realized household welfare gains.
Infrastructure gains are long run and uneven.

evidence.claim: The government said Plano Safra 2022/23 would provide R$340.88 billion in rural credit, up 36% from the previous plan.
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock / Government of Brazil
evidence.excerpt: The government said Plano Safra 2022/23 would provide R$340.88 billion in rural credit, up 36% from the previous plan.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: This is the official launch page for the 2022/23 rural credit program, with the stated amount and percentage increase.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct government policy under Bolsonaro, though sectoral benefits are concentrated in agriculture rather than the whole economy.
contrary_evidence: Sectoral credit expansion can help productivity but does not prove broad household welfare gains.
Agricultural output can also be exposed to commodity and weather cycles.

evidence.claim: The federal government reported a 2022 primary surplus of R$59.7 billion, above the year's formal projection.
evidence.title: Governo Federal apresenta superávit primário de R$ 59,7 bilhões em 2022
evidence.excerpt: The federal government reported a 2022 primary surplus of R$59.7 billion, above the year's formal projection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: National Treasury is the authoritative source for the official fiscal outcome and the release gives the final figure directly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to the Bolsonaro administration's fiscal choices, but the result also reflects one-offs, transfers, and revenue conditions beyond his control.
contrary_evidence: A surplus does not erase election-year spending expansion or inflation pressure.
The headline result may not reflect underlying sustainability or quality of spending.

The original TSE-filed 2022 program is only indirectly represented here through a secondary summary.
